Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking an Electrical Commissioning Engineer to execute the buildout, startup, and handover of electrical systems for SpaceXAI's high-performance data centers. This is a hands-on role where you will commission, test, troubleshoot, and turn over critical systems that support next-generation AI supercomputing infrastructure.

You will work closely with construction, engineering, operations, EPC contractors, and OEM vendors to deliver safe, reliable, and high-quality electrical systems. This is a full-time, onsite role with travel to SpaceXAI data center construction sites across the United States.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Execute all electrical commissioning activities for MV/LV switchgear, generators, UPS systems, PDUs, ATS/STS, transformers, relays, busway, and associated controls in hyperscale data center environments.
• Execute functional performance testing, pre-functional testing, site acceptance testing, load-bank testing, protection-relay testing, integrated system testing, and system turnover to operations.
• Troubleshoot and resolve complex electrical, controls, and process issues during pre-commissioning, commissioning, and startup phases.
• Develop and review detailed commissioning test procedures, scripts, checklists, and documentation in alignment with project specifications, industry standards, and SpaceXAI requirements.
• Coordinate with EPC contractors, OEM vendors, design engineers, and SpaceXAI stakeholders for system energization, startup sequences, and integrated system validation.
• Champion safety by enforcing strict adherence to LOTO, NFPA, OSHA, and SpaceXAI safety protocols; participate in daily safety briefings and job hazard analyses.
• Maintain comprehensive as-built documentation, test records, issue logs, and final commissioning reports.
• Support and deliver training programs for operations and maintenance teams on commissioned systems.
• Participate in constructability reviews, design feedback sessions, and lessons-learned meetings to continuously improve installation quality and future project execution.
• Support commissioning schedules and punch-list resolution to meet aggressive project timelines.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering.
• 5+ years of experience in commissioning for electrical systems.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Working knowledge of commissioning test equipment (power analyzers, insulation testers, hipot testers, torque tools, IR cameras, load banks, relay test sets, etc.), or demonstrated aptitude to learn it in the field.
• Familiarity with relevant codes and standards (NEC, NFPA 70/70B/70E, IEEE, NETA, NESC, Uptime Institute).
• Ability to read, interpret, and redline electrical drawings, one-lines, three-lines, control schematics, and sequence of operations; update as-built models after commissioning.
• Experience coordinating with multi-discipline teams, contractors, and vendors in construction environments.
• Ability to work safely in industrial construction environments and follow LOTO, NFPA, OSHA, and SpaceXAI safety protocols.
• Commissioning experience, including functional performance testing, pre-functional testing, site acceptance testing, load-bank testing, protection-relay testing, integrated system testing, and system turnover.
• Data center systems and prior work on mission-critical projects
• Hands-on experience with EPMS, BMS/BAS, and power-system controls troubleshooting and integration (Modbus, BACnet, etc.).
• Knowledge of refrigerant systems, direct liquid cooling, and advanced heat rejection technologies.
• Current OSHA 30 certification or equivalent.
• Proficiency with commissioning management platforms (CxPro, Procore, PlanGrid, or similar).
• Experience implementing integrated systems testing, owner’s project requirements verification, and feeding as-built data back into the sitewide power model (load flow, short-circuit, coordination, arc-flash).

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Willingness to travel extensively and work extended hours, nights, and weekends during critical commissioning and startup windows.
• Ability to travel extensively to SpaceXAI construction sites and remain onsite for extended periods during peak commissioning phases.
• Physical capability to work in industrial environments, climb ladders/stairs, lift moderate loads (up to 50 lbs), and wear full PPE for long durations.
• Valid driver’s license and ability to meet SpaceXAI's driver eligibility requirements.

The Supplier Risk Manager is a senior-level role within Global Supplier Management (GSM), part of the Global Procurement Organization (GPO). This role owns the end-to-end design, development, and operationalization of supplier risk programs and policies protecting Amazon's global supply chain across ~$45B in annual spend.
You will architect comprehensive risk programs and establish the governance frameworks, analytics infrastructure, and resource models that enable scalable execution. The ideal candidate is a builder who thrives in ambiguity, defines both the “what” and the “how,” and drives cross-functional alignment at enterprise scale.

Key job responsibilities
Program Architecture & Execution
• Design and implement scalable supplier risk programs spanning financial, operational, reputational, safety, regulatory, tier-n, geopolitical, sustainability, and single/sole source risk domains
• Develop risk scoring methodologies, segmentation frameworks, and tiered monitoring approaches aligned to supplier criticality and spend exposure
• Build early warning systems to proactively identify emerging supplier risks before business impact occurs
• Consolidate siloed risk management activities into a unified, governed program portfolio with defined escalation pathways, response protocols, and supplier remediation frameworks
• Define program success metrics, reporting cadences, and escalation protocols
• Identify and secure resource support structures — team capacity, partner ownership, technology tools, or vendor support — that enable programs to operate at scale

Policy Development & Governance
• Author and maintain supplier risk management policies, standards, and procedures enabling consistent execution across all regions
• Establish governance mechanisms to ensure policy compliance and drive continuous improvement
• Partner with Legal, Compliance, GPO partners, and Finance to ensure alignment with regulatory requirements and corporate standards
• Own policy lifecycle management including periodic reviews, updates, and stakeholder communication

Stakeholder Engagement & Influence
• Collaborate with Category Managers, Supplier Performance Managers, and regional teams to embed risk considerations into sourcing decisions, business consequence decisions, and supplier lifecycle management
• Present risk posture, program performance, and policy recommendations to senior leadership
• Influence cross-functional partners without direct authority to adopt risk management practices and tools
• Champion a risk-aware culture across GSM and the broader GPO

Analytics & Continuous Improvement
• Lead design of data models and risk scoring methodologies integrating financial health assessments, background/suitability screening, ESG indicators, geopolitical signals, safety records, quality metrics, capacity, delivery, and other performance metrics
• Leverage data and analytics to identify risk trends, concentration risks, and portfolio vulnerabilities
• Drive automation and tooling improvements to increase program scalability and reduce manual effort
• Benchmark internal practices against industry standards and implement leading-edge approaches

A day in the life
• Global scope supporting all regions
• High degree of autonomy with expectation to define both strategy and execution
• Cross-functional collaboration with Category Management, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Security, Sustainability, and Operations teams
• Hybrid work environment; travel up to 50%

About the team
GSM is comprised of multi-disciplinary experts in quality assurance, supplier qualifications, operational excellence, and new product qualifications. We identify and mitigate supplier risk before it impacts Amazon's supply chain, executing detailed assessments and risk programs across the full supplier lifecycle. Our team is passionate about innovation, continuous improvement, and building programs as durable and scalable as the supply chains we support.

Manager, Fixed Equipment Reliability

The Manager, Fixed Equipment Reliability (FER Manager) is a technical second-line management and senior engineering position responsible for the refinery’s fixed equipment engineering, corrosion and materials engineering, and assigned reliability engineering functions.

The FER Manager leads a multidisciplinary team and serves as the senior engineer and technical resource for the group, providing technical leadership, senior-level review, and strategic direction to improve safety, mechanical integrity, equipment availability, risk reduction, maintainability, and lifecycle cost performance across the refinery. The FER Manager recognizes and draws upon the specialized experience and expertise of individual team members while maintaining broad technical oversight of the group’s work.

The FER Manager works across Operations, Maintenance, Inspection, Projects, Turnarounds, and company technical networks to establish fixed equipment strategies, develop long-range asset plans, manage corrosion and degradation risks, address chronic equipment issues, and support safe and reliable refinery operations.

Safety and Process Safety Leadership

• Champion the refinery safety culture and ensure activities are conducted in accordance with company safety policies and procedures.

• Ensure fixed equipment engineering activities comply with applicable regulatory requirements, recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices (RAGAGEP), and company and refinery standards.

• Ensure appropriate technical support is provided for process safety events, incident investigations, and root cause failure analyses involving fixed equipment, corrosion, materials, and related reliability issues, participating directly when warranted.

Leadership and People Management

• Lead and develop assigned fixed equipment engineering, corrosion and materials engineering, reliability engineering, and other technical personnel.

• Establish performance expectations and provide coaching, mentoring, technical guidance, senior-level technical review, and career development opportunities.

• Conduct performance reviews and succession-planning activities.

• Develop staffing strategies and participate in recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and resource planning efforts, including use of contract technical support when appropriate.

• Ensure training and development plans are established and followed for team members.

Mechanical Integrity and Asset Management

• Provide leadership for the refinery’s fixed equipment mechanical integrity and reliability programs, including pressure vessels, piping, tanks, heat exchangers, fired equipment, and other assigned fixed assets.

• Develop and execute strategies that improve equipment integrity and availability, manage degradation risk, reduce unplanned downtime and loss of containment potential, and optimize lifecycle cost.

• Provide engineering leadership for corrosion management, materials selection, damage-mechanism reviews, integrity operating windows, risk-based inspection, fitness-for-service evaluations, repair strategies, and remaining-life assessments.

• Use inspection findings, equipment condition, corrosion data, failure history, and risk information to prioritize improvements and communicate key indicators, trends, and concerns to business team stakeholders and refinery leadership.

• Govern fixed equipment criticality, lifecycle planning, obsolescence management, and long-term repair or replacement strategies.

• Coordinate with Operations, Maintenance, and Inspection to improve equipment performance through effective operating practices, inspection plans, preventive maintenance, monitoring, and timely corrective action.

• Elevate significant or unresolved equipment risks, overdue actions, resource needs, and integrity concerns to refinery leadership when warranted.

Technical Oversight

• Ensure the team proactively engages with Operations, Maintenance, and Inspection departments to identify, evaluate, and resolve emerging and recurring fixed equipment issues. Provide direct technical support and leadership for complex, high-risk, or cross-functional issues when warranted.

• Serve as a senior technical resource to the group by reviewing and challenging significant engineering evaluations, repair recommendations, risk assessments, and technical decisions, while appropriately leveraging subject-matter expertise within the team and company technical networks.

• Ensure appropriate engineering resources are provided to support equipment design, repair development, materials selection, welding and fabrication requirements, technical quality assurance, commissioning, and startup activities.

• Support Management of Change (MOC) activities and perform or assign senior technical reviews and technical approvals as required, with particular attention to complex, high-risk, or non-routine changes.

• Steward consistent application of applicable API and ASME codes, company and refinery standards, risk-based decision-making, fitness-for-service, failure analysis, and lifecycle cost analysis methodologies. Ensure significant technical work is appropriately reviewed based on complexity, risk, and the experience of the assigned engineer.

• Maintain clear technical interfaces among Fixed Equipment Engineering, Inspection, Operations, Maintenance, Projects, and Turnarounds, including ownership and timely closure of recommendations and action items.

Turnarounds and Capital Projects

• Ensure integrity-driven work scopes and capital improvements are identified, developed, justified, and advanced through the appropriate refinery turnaround or capital-planning process.

• Ensure inspection findings, corrosion risks, repair requirements, maintainability, standardization, lifecycle cost, and long-term equipment needs are incorporated into turnaround scopes and capital projects.

• Ensure qualified technical resources support scope development, design reviews, repair plans, technical evaluations, execution, quality assurance, commissioning, startup, and post-startup performance verification, as applicable.

• Provide fixed equipment technical leadership for major outages and turnarounds, serving as the technical lead when appropriate.

Business and Financial Management

• Develop and manage budgets for assigned fixed equipment engineering, corrosion and materials, and reliability activities.

• Prioritize engineering resources to align with refinery safety, mechanical integrity, operational risk, reliability, and business objectives.

• Develop multiyear forecasts for major repairs, lifecycle replacements, corrosion mitigation, reliability improvements, and risk-reduction initiatives.

• Track and report mechanical integrity and reliability performance indicators and the operational and financial value associated with improvement initiatives.

• Support refinery business planning through development of annual and multiyear fixed equipment asset improvement plans.

Corporate and Industry Engagement

• Represent the refinery in applicable company fixed equipment, mechanical integrity, corrosion and materials, and reliability technical networks and ensure appropriate site participation and support.

• Maintain awareness of emerging technologies, applicable industry practices, regulatory requirements, and lessons learned relevant to fixed equipment integrity.

• Develop and maintain productive relationships with technical peers across the company and industry.

JOB QUALIFICATION

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in engineering from an accredited institution.

• Minimum of 7 years of experience in fixed equipment, mechanical integrity, inspection, corrosion and materials, or related engineering work in refining, petrochemical processing, or a comparable industrial environment.

• Previous supervisory experience or a demonstrated record of successfully leading technical personnel and multidisciplinary work.

• Strong leadership and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively across Operations, Maintenance, Inspection, Engineering, Turnarounds, Capital Projects, and refinery leadership.

• Broad working knowledge of fixed equipment engineering, corrosion and materials, inspection, and reliability functions within a refinery or comparable operating facility, with the technical judgment to review significant work and support complex or high-risk issues.

• Demonstrated ability to manage a large and changing workload, establish priorities, and allocate resources based on safety, equipment risk, operational impact, and business value.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly communicate technical risks, priorities, and recommendations.

• Demonstrated commitment to safety, personal integrity, accountability, and operational excellence.

About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

We are seeking Engineering Technicians to support the assembly, testing, and prototyping of custom electromechanical actuators for advanced robotic systems. You will build and test hardware from engineering drawings and procedures through inspection, troubleshooting, and rework, partnering closely with mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, and test engineers.

These roles focus on hands-on work with precision electromechanical hardware, including stator prototypes, motor and actuator assemblies, and mechanical and electrical testing. You will help turn engineering designs into validated hardware while improving build records, work instructions, and repeatable assembly and test practices for future robotic platforms.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 5 days a week.

In this role, you will:

Each opening focuses on actuator builds, testing, or stator prototyping, with responsibilities aligned to the selected specialty.

- Actuator builds: assemble subassemblies and complete actuators from drawings, bills of materials, and work instructions, checking fit, orientation, torque, routing, and workmanship.

- Testing: set up and run established mechanical and electrical tests, confirm the setup against the procedure, record measurements, and identify unexpected results.

- Stator prototyping: support winding, insulation, termination, bonding, inspection, and rework using the selected build process and documented instructions.

- Troubleshoot build and test issues with engineers. Isolate problems through inspection and measurement, escalate deviations, and verify the result after approved rework.

- Maintain accurate build and test records, part and revision traceability, inspection results, and rework history.

- Use bench observations to improve work instructions, fixtures, tooling, and parts organization as prototypes evolve.

- Follow safety, ESD, cleanliness, and quality practices, and communicate material shortages, unclear instructions, and other blockers as priorities change.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have hands-on experience building or testing mechanical, electrical, or electromechanical hardware in a lab, prototype shop, or manufacturing environment.

- Can work from drawings, bills of materials, wiring diagrams, and procedures, and recognize when the instructions and hardware do not agree.

- Use hand tools, torque tools, and measurement equipment carefully, with consistent workmanship and attention to units and acceptance limits.

- Troubleshoot methodically, document observations, and know when to pause work and ask for engineering support.

- Take ownership of build quality and records while adapting to changing designs and priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

About the Role

Our Technical Deployment Leads (TDLs) and Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) embed with strategic customers to ship production AI applications that solve real business problems. Our delivery model pairs two roles: FDEs own the technical artifact, and TDLs own the engagement end-to-end — from statement of work (SOW) through production deployment.

As a Manager of Technical Deployment for Financial Services, you own engagement portfolio health across your vertical. You set the bar for delivery quality and build the playbooks and evaluation frameworks that let the practice scale. Your work will directly influence Anthropic's product direction and establish Anthropic as the trusted partner for AI transformation across the Fortune 100.

This is a player-coach role. You need to be credible in architecture conversations with a customer's engineering leads and equally comfortable in sales conversations in front of executive sponsors, and you will lead the most complex engagements yourself when the stakes call for it. Most of your impact will come through the people you hire and the standard you hold them to. You won't write production code, but you will pressure-test the technical decisions your TDL team makes with FDEs.

Responsibilities

• Hire, develop, and retain a team of TDLs embedded in Financial Services engagements. Set a high bar for delivery judgment, technical fluency, and customer presence, and run the interviews that hold it.
• Manage each TDL directly: regular 1:1s, clear expectations, direct feedback, and a growth plan. Build a bench that runs engagements well without you in the room.
• Own portfolio health across the vertical. Track which engagements are on track, at risk, or closing out, and intervene early when delivery drifts. Run engagement quality reviews with your team.
• Own customer outcomes across the portfolio. Hold the executive relationship with customer sponsors, run steering committees, and represent Anthropic's credibility with senior business, risk, and engineering leaders.
• Make the staffing call for each engagement. Work with FDE managers to match TDLs and engineers to each customer, and adjust as scope changes.
• Lead the most complex engagements yourself. Take the TDL seat when engagement size, regulatory exposure, or organizational complexity calls for it, from delivery plan through production.
• Set the bar for delivery excellence — SOW quality, MVP scoping, and value measurement. Ensure every engagement has a defensible impact story.
• Codify reusable solution patterns, evaluation frameworks, and technical playbooks across the team. Turn what works in the field into delivery infrastructure that lets the practice scale.
• Partner with Sales to qualify engagements, shape scope, and inform SOWs. Partner with Marketing and Sales on Financial Services–specific go-to-market materials, reference cases, and positioning.
• Run the team's operating rhythm: engagement reviews, knowledge-sharing, and escalation support, and report into the wider post-sales cadence and dashboards. Set team goals tied to customer outcomes.
• Bring the field back to Anthropic. Surface delivery lessons and emerging Financial Services use cases to Product and Research, and represent the vertical in leadership discussions.
• Consistently uphold Anthropic's values as you lead your team. TDLs should be strong representatives of Anthropic's culture as they work within customer environments.
• Travel to customer sites (25–50% expected).

You May Be a Good Fit If You

• Have 8+ years leading enterprise AI/ML delivery, whether you came up as a founder, engineer, data scientist, or researcher who has moved into deployments, with at least 3 years directly managing people who owned delivery outcomes.
• Have a track record of building and leading technical delivery teams in enterprise environments, ideally including embedded or forward-deployed teams working at client sites.
